Short title extent and commencement

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
1. Short title,
extent and commencement.-(I) This Ordinance may be called the War Risks
Insurance Ordinance, 1965.
(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan,
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Definitions

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
2. Definition.-In
this Ordinance, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,-
(a) "agricultural
products" means products of agriculture, horticulture, or sylviculture,
and includes growing crops, plants and trees ;
(b)
"building" includes foundations, boundary walls, plinths, garages,
floors, staircases, tanks, engine and boiler beds, chimneys, and flues ;
(c) "factory"
means a factory as defined in clause (j) of section 2 of the Factories Act,
1934 (XXV of 1934), and includes any premises including the precincts thereof
which having at any time on or after the commencement of this Ordinance been
such factory ;
(d) "Factory
buildings" include all buildings comprised in the factory (and such other
buildings including residential buildings for staff and workmen, hospitals and
welfare centres) within a radius of two miles from the main factory building as
are in the same ownership or occupation as the factory and are used for the
purpose of the factory ;
(e) "Funds" means a
War Risks Insurance Fund established under section 17 ;
(.f) " goods "
means any materials, commodities or articles and includes materials or articles
used in or for the construction of ships up to the time at which a ship after
construction is launched but does not include a ship ;
(g) " insurable value
" in relation to any property means the value of the property as
ascertained for the purpose of insurance under this Ordinance ;
(h) "
live-stock " includes animals of any description ;
(i) " occupier " in
relation to a factory has the meaning assigned to the words in clause (1) of
section 2 of the Factories Act, 1934 (XXV of 1934) ;
(j) " owner " in relation to a factory
or building, when parts of the property insurable under this Ordinance in
relation to such factory or building are owned by different persons, each such
person in respect of the part owned by him ;
(k) "
prescribed " means prescribed by rules, made under this Ordinance ;
(1) " property insurable under this Ordinance "-
(i) in relation to any factory,
means the factory building and, except where they are goods mentioned in section
3 as goods insurable under this Ordinance, all plant and machinery in the
factory and such other plant and machinery as may be prescribed ;
(ii) in relation to any
building, includes plinths, floors, staircases, tanks or any immovable
construction which form part of the building ; and
(iii) in relation to any ship,
includes hull, machinery, tackle, and except where they are goods mentioned in
section 3 as goods insurable under this Ordinance, goods carried therein ;
(m) "Scheme " means a
War Risks Insurance Scheme prepared under section 6 ;
(n) "seller of goods
" includes a seller of goods acting as an agent, and in relation to any
person carrying on the business of selling goods as an agent, any reference in
this Ordinance to goods produced by him or to goods not produced by him shall
be construed as including a reference to goods produced, or as the case may be,
not produced by his principal ;
(o) " ship " means
any ship registered in Pakistan and includes any machinery, tackle, furniture
and goods carried therein, not being goods mentioned in section 3 as goods
insurable under this Ordinance ;
(p) "
war risks " means such risks as may be prescribed arising from-
(i) action taken by an enemy or
action taken in combating an enemy or in repelling an imagined attack by an
enemy ;
(ii) any explosion or fire
which involves any explosive or munitions or other dangerous things required
for war purposes and which happens, or is caused by, through or in connection
with, the manufacture, storage or transportation of any such explosives
munitions or other dangerous thi

Goods insurable under this ordinance

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
3. Goods insurable under
this Ordinance.-(1) The following goods shall be deemed to be goods
insurable under this Ordinance, namely :-
(a) in relation to any person
carrying on business in Pakistan as a seller .of goods of any description
produced by him, all goods situated in Pakistan being either-
(i) goods of that description,
or
(ii) goods, including those irk
process, used as material from which goods of that description are produced, or as
ingredients or components parts of goods of that description ;
(b) in relation to any person
carrying on business in Pakistan as a seller of goods of any description not
produced by him, all goods of that description situated in Pakistan ;
(c) in relation to any person carrying
on business in. Pakistan as a seller of goods, all such goods as are described
in clauses (a) and (b) while they are in transit .between places within
Pakistan or between a place outside Pakistan and a place in Pakistan ;
(d) in relation to a person
carrying on the business in Pakistan - of selling agricultural products
produced by him, all agricultural products and live-stock -for the time being
situated in Pakistan in respect of which he is the producer, seller or owner.
(2) Goods which, in relation to
a person carrying on any business as a seller of goods, are at any time
insurable under this Ordinance, shall not cease to be so insurable by reason
only that they are subsequently placed in or fixed to land under a contract of
sale entered into by that person in the course of that business.
(3.) For the purpose of clause
(c) of subsection (1), goods shall be deemed to be in transit till they reach
the intended destination and are discharged by the carrier.
(4) The Central Government may,
by notification in the official Gazette, direct that goods of any description
specified - in the notification shall, notwithstanding anything contained in
this section, be-deemed not to be goods insurable under this Ordinance.

Ownership in relation to goods

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
4. Ownership in relation to goods.-Save
as otherwise provided in this Ordinance, any goods shall, for the purposes of
this Ordinance, be deemed to be owned,-
(a) if the property in the
goods is for the. time being vested in a person in relation to whom they are
insurable undr this Ordinance by that person ;
(b) if the property in the
goods is not so vested, by any person in relation to whom the goods are
insurable under this Ordinance and who is for the time being entitled either
unconditionally or conditionally, to have the property in the goods vested in
him
Provided that any goods shall
be deemed to be owned by a person carry ing on business in Pakistan who is, for
the time being, entitled to sell the goods as an agent if such goods are, under
the foregoing provisions of this section, deemed to be owned by a person-
(i) in whom the property
therein is vested otherwise than in the course of a business carried on by him
in Pakistan,- or
(ii) who is entitled to
have property therein vested in him otherwise than in the course of such a
business.

Ownership in relation to ships under construction

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
5. Ownership in
relation to ships, under construction.-(1) where in the course of any
business a ship is being, or has been, constructed under contr act and the ship
or any part thereof or any goods appropriate for the construction thereof
would,-
(a) apart from the
provisions of this subsection, have been deemed for the purposes of this
Ordinance to be owned at any time by the person from time to time carrying on
the business ; or
(b) have at any time
been accepted,. in pursuance of a contract made with him, by the person from
time to time carrying on the business, then, notwithstanding that they would
not, apart from the said provisions, be deemed for the said purpose to be owned
by the person from time to time carrying on the business, the ship and any part
thereof and any goods so appropriated as aforesaid shall, subject to the
provisions of subsec tion (2), be deemed,-
(i) to continue to be
owned, in a case to which clause (a) applies, by the person from time to time
carrying on the business until the acceptance of the ship in pursuance of the
contract in question, and
(ii) to be owned, in a case
to which clause (b) applies,
by the person from time to time carrying on the business at all times between
the acceptance referred to in that clause and the acceptance of the ship as
aforesaid by the person for whom it is being, or has been, constructed.
(2) The
provisions of subsection (1) shall apply in relation to the construction under
contract in the course of a business of part of a ship, not being part of a
ship which is being, or has been constructed by the person from time to time
carrying on the business, as they apply in, relation to the construction of a
ship=
(a) with the
substitution for reference to a ship of reference 0 part of a ship ;
(b) where the
contract for the part of the ship is with the person for whom the ship is being
constructed, with the substitution for references to the acceptance of the ship
under the contract in question of references to the acceptance of the ship
under contract for the construction thereof ;
(c) where -the
contract for the part of the ship is with any other person, with the
substitution for references to the acceptance of the ship under the contract in
question of references to the acceptance of the part of the ship under the
contract, for the construction of the part by the person for whom it is being,
or has been, constructed.
(3) Where the
person from time to time carrying on a business re ceives any money, under a
policy of insurance issued under this Ordinance in respect of loss of or damage
to a ship, part of a ship or goods which are deemed to be owned by him by
virtue of subsection (1) or subsection (2), the money shall be held by him on
trust for the person who apart from the provisions of those subsections would
be deemed for the purposes of this Ordinance to be the owner of the ship, part
of a ship or goods subject however to any lien or charge which would otherwise
be enforceable against the ship, part or goods and subject also to the right to
retain out of the money the amount of any expenses reasonably incurred by the
firs mentioned person in making good any part of the loss or damage which he is liable to make good.

War risks insurance scheme

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
6. War Risks Insurance
Scheme.-(1) The Central Government ma prepare one or more War Risks
Insurance Schemes whereby it undertake in relation to any goods or property
insurable under this Ordinance the liabilities of insuring against war risk
subject to the provisions of, and t( the extent provided by or under, this
Ordinance, and may, by notification in the official Gazette put into operation
any such Scheme which shall b published with such notification.
(2) Any Scheme prepared under
subsection` (1) shall be such as t( secure-
(a) that the liability of the
Central Government as insurer shall no exceed such percentage of insurable
value of the goods or property as may b~ prescribed in relation to any goods or
property or any class of goods o property ;
(b) that in respect of each claim the insured
shall bear such percentage of loss or damage as may be prescribed in relation
to and goods or property or any class of goods or property, or such other
amount as may be fixed with reference to the insurable value of the good or
property in accordance with the prescribed scale whichever is greater ;
(c) that any liability of the
Central Government as insurer in relation to any goods or property
is determined- by the policy of insurance issued by , person acting n behalf
of the Central Government in such form and for such period as may be prescribed
in relation to such goods or property under different circumstances ; .
(d) that any premium under a
policy so issued is payable at such rate and the amount of any one such premium
is not less than such sum, as may from time to time, be prescribed for
different description of goods or different kinds of property, in respect of
different periods and under different circumstances.
(3) When the rate of premium
prescribed in relation to any policy o class of policies for any period fixed
for the purpose is altered during the continuance of such policies, the rate so
altered shall be the rate applicable to all policies, under which premiums are
payable in respect of that period notwithstanding that the policies may have
been issued on payment o premium at the rate in force before the alteration ;
and any policy issued of payment at the rate in force before the
alteration, shall, when the rate has been increased by such alteration, cease
to be valid on such date as may b fixed in this behalf by the Central
Government unless before such date an deficiency in the amount paid as premium
is made good by the policy holder. . .

Scheme with respect to property

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
7. Scheme with respect to
property.-Any Scheme with respect to an; property insurable under this
Ordinance may provide-
(a) for undertaking in relation
to works in course of. construction which when completed will become a property
insurable under this Ordinance, the same liabilities as are undertaken by the
Scheme appertaining to such property ;
(b) that the payments due under
a policy of insurance issued under the Scheme may, at the option of the Central
Government, take either of the following forms, namely :-
(i) payment, within the limit
of the liability assumed by the Central Government in such manner and by such
instalments, as the Central Government may think fit, of the cost necessary to
restore the property as far as practicable to the condition in which it existed
before the occurrence of the damage, or
(ii) compensation, within the aforesaid limits, for the
loss in value ascertained on the basis of value and prices ruling at the time
at which the policy of insurance was taken out, or at which the loss occurred,
whichever is less, suffered by the property as a result of the damage, after
due allowance has been made for depreciation during the current period of
insurance cover ;
(c) for the
postponement, in accordance with such principles and under such circumstances
as may be prescribed, of payments due under a policy of insurance issued under
the Scheme in respect of any damage sustained by property insured thereunder ;
(d) for making it a
condition of any policy of insurance issued under the Scheme-
(i) that the owner or
occupier of a property shall comply with all regula tions or instructions made
or issued under the authority of Government for safeguarding the property
against damage from war risks ; or
(ii) that, where the
Central Government exercises its option to pay the cost necessary to restore
the property to its .original condition, the owner of the property shall, if so
required by the Central Government, repair or re construct the property or
remove it in another locality and reconstruct thereon.

Scheme with respect to goods

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
8. Scheme with
respect to goods.-Any Scheme with respect to any goods may extend-
(a) to the undertaking
by the Central Government, in relation to any person carrying on business in Pakistan
as a seller of goods, of the liability of insuring such a person against war
risks in respect of goods insurable under this Ordinance which are not owned by
him but in which he has an interest arising in the course of that business ;
(b) to the undertaking
by the Central Government, in relation to a person carrying on any business in
Pakistan, without prejudice to the provis ions of clause (a), of the liability
of insuring such a person against war risks in respect of-
(i) any goods
situated in Pakistan which are in his possession, otherwise than under a hire
purchase agreement, for the .purposes of that business, and.
(ii) any goods situated
in Pakistan which are subject to a mortgage in his favour, held by him in the
course of that business, being in either case ,goods which are not owned, by
him but which are insurable under this Ordin ance in relation to the person by
whom they are owned.;
(c) to the
undertaking by the Central Government, in relation to a person carrying on any business
in Pakistan, of the liability of insuring such a person against war risks with
respect to any goods, situated in Pakistan which, having been sold in Pakistan,
for export from Pakistan are in his possession for the purpose of such export
and are goods which were, prior to such sale, insurable under this Ordinance
in. relation to the person by whom they were then owned;
(d) to the
undertaking by the Central Government, in relation to any person carrying on
business in Pakistan as a seller of goods, of the liability of insuring such
person against war risks in respect of goods imported into Pakistan through any
port, while such goods are situated at such
port or are in transit from such port to a place in Pakistan;
(e) to the
undertaking by the Central Government, in relation to a Provincial Government,
of the liability of insuring the Provincial Government in such special cases as
it thinks fit against war risks with respect to goods for the time being owned
by the Provincial Government, which are goods that would be goods insurable
under this Ordinance if the Provincial Government were a person carrying on
business in Pakistan as a seller of goods of that description.

Extent of scheme with respect to property

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
9. Extent of Scheme with respect to property.-Any
Scheme with respect to property insurable under this Ordinance may extend to
the undertaking by the Central Government, in relation to any person in
Pakistan, of the liability of insuring such person against war risks with
respect to any such property which is not owned by him but in which he has an
interest up to the extent of such interest.

Compulsory insurance of goods

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
10. Compulsory
insurance of goods.-(1) No person shall, after such date as the Central
Government may, by notification in the official Gazette specify, carry on any
business in Pakistan as a seller of goods, unless, with respect to any goods
insurable under this Ordinance which are for the time being owned by him in the
course of that business, there is in force a policy of insurance against war
risks issued in accordance with the Scheme relating to such goods.
(2) The provisions of subsection (1) shall not apply-
(i) to the
carrying on of business as aforesaid by any person, if and so long as the value
of all goods insurable under this Ordinance, other than goods in transit
referred to in clause (c) of subsection (1) of, section 3, which are for the
time being owned by him within one and the same district in the course of that
business, does not exceed such amount as may be prescribed in this behalf but,
if the Central Government, by notification in the official Gazette, so directs,
such person may be insured, if he so wishes at a rate double the rate
prescribed for a policy relating to such goods, the amount of any one premium payable
under a policy issued to him being not less than double the amount prescribed
for such policy
(ii) to the carrying on
of business as aforesaid by any person with respect to goods of any description
specified in such notification other than goods in transit referred to in
clause (c) of subsection (1) of section 3 ; if the Central Government, by
notification in the official Gazette, so declares; and
(iii) to any person
referred to in clause (d) of subsection (1) of section 3 with respect to goods
which, apart from the provisions of that clause, would not be goods insurable
under this Ordinance, if the Central Govern ment, by general or special order,
so directs.
(3) Whoever contravenes
the -provisions of subsection (1) shall be punishable with fine which may
extend to five hundred rupees and with a further fine which may extend to one
thousand rupees for every day after the first on which the contravention
continues.
sections.punishment:
punishable with fine which may
extend to five hundred rupees and with a further fine which may extend to one
thousand rupees for every day after the first on which the contravention
continues.

sections.description:
Compulsory insurance of factory

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
11. Compulsory insurance
of factory.-(1) Every owner of a factory, except a factory belonging to the
Central Government or the Provincial Government or a factory exempted under subsection (2) from
the pro visions of this subsection, shall, by such date as the Central Government
may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify in this behalf, take out
a policy of insurance against war risks issued in accordance with the Scheme
whereby he is insured in respect of all property which appertains to the
factory for a sum not less than the insurable value of such property
Provided that, where
the owner of the factory is not himself the occupier of the factory, the
occupier of the factory shall, unless the owner has already taken out a policy
of insurance as required by this subsection, himself take out the policy and in
such a case the occupier shall be deemed to act as the agent of the owner and
shall be entitled to receive from the owner all sums paid as premiums on the
policy.
(2) The
Central Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, exempt any
factory or any description of factories or any pre mises including the
precincts hereof which have at any time after the commencement of this
Ordinance been a factory as defined in clause (j) of section 2 of the Factories
Act, 1934 (XXV of 1934), froze the provisions of this section and may by order
declare that any factory or any description of factories so exempted may, if
the owner so wishes, b8 insured under the Scheme.

Compulsory insurance of buildings

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
12. Compulsory insurance
of buildings.-(1) Every owner of a build ing, except a building owned by
the Central Government or the Pro vincial Government, shall, by such date as
the Central Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify in
this behalf, take out a policy of insurance against war risks issued in
accordance with the Scheme whereby he is insured in respect of all property
insurable under this Ordinance which appertains to the building for a sum not
less than the insurable value of such property.
(2) Subsection (1)
shall not apply to owners of buildings of an insur able value less than an
amount as may be prescribed in this behalf, but if the Central Government, by a
notification in the official Gazette, so directs, any such owner may insure his
property, i he so wishes, at a rate of premium double the rate prescribed for
a policy relating to such building.

Compulsory insurance of ship

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
13. Compulsory insurance
of ship.-(1) Every owner of a ship except a ship owned by the Central
Government or the Provincial Government, shall, by such date as the Central
Government may, by notification in the official. Gazette, specify in this
behalf, take out a policy of insurance against war risks for a sum not less
than the insurable value of such ship.
(2) Subsection
(1) shall rot apply to owners of ships of such des cription and of an insurable
value less than such amount as may be pres cribed in this behalf, but if the
Central Government, by a notification in the official Gazette. so directs, any
such owner may insure his ship, if he so wishes, at a rate of premium double
the rate prescribed for a policy relating to such ship.
(3) The Central
Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct that all ships
exempted under subsection (2) and owned by a Provincial Government or by a
Corporation established under any Central or Provincial law shall be insured at
such rate of premium as may be prescribed from time to time in this behalf, and
thereupon all provisions applicable to owners of ships shall apply to such
owners.

Obligation under sections 11 12 and 13 includes obligation to insure repaired or reconstructed property

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
14. Obligation
under sections 11, 12 and 13 includes obligation to insure repaired or
reconstructed property.-The obligation imposed by section 11, section 12 or
section 13 includes, where the owner of a property insured under this Ordinance
is required by the Central Government to
repair or reconstruct such property which has suffered
damage, an obliga tion to take out an additional policy of insurance as
required by those sections in respect of the property so repaired or
reconstructed.

Penalty for contravention of section  11 12 and 13

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
15. Penalty
for contravention of sections 11, 12 and 13.-When insur ance of a property
is obligatory, whoever contravenes the provisions of section 11, section 12 .or
section 13 or having taken out a policy of insurance fails to pay any
instalment of premium thereon which is sub sequently due shall be punishable
with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees for every day after the first
on which the contravention or failure continues.
sections.punishment:
punishable
with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees for every day after the first
on which the contravention or failure continues.

sections.description:
Transfer of property insured under this ordinance

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
16. Transfer
of property insured under this Ordinance.-(1) When a property in respect of
which a policy of insurance is obligatory and has been taken out as is required
by this Ordinance is. transferred from one owner to another or there is a
change of occupier of such property, the policy may, subject to rules, if any,
made in this behalf, be transferred to the new owner or occupier, and ,such new
owner or occupier shall succeed to all rights, and liabilities under and in
relation to the policy as if the policy had been in the first instance taken
out by him.
(2) When a
property in respect of which a policy of insurance is not obligatory, but has
been taken out voluntarily, is transferred from one owner to another the policy
shall cease' to take effect from the date of such, transfer and no refund of
premium shall be made to the transferor.

War risks insurance fund

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
17. War Risks
Insurance Fund.-(1) The Central Government, shall establish a Fund to be
called War Risks Insurance Fund in which shall be paid all sums received by the
Central Government by way of insurance premiums under any Scheme or by way of
payments made on composition of offences under this Ordinance and out of which
shall be paid all sums required for the discharge by the Central Government of
any of its liabilities under any Scheme or for the payment by the Central
Government of the remunera tion and expenses of agents employed under section
19.
(2) Where the
Central Government requires the owner of any property insured under this
Ordinance to repair the property or to remove and reconstruct it in another
place, it shall make to such owner out of the Fund such payment, in addition to
any sum payable under the policy of insurance, as it considers sufficient to
defray the cost of repair, removal or reconstruction, and, if necessary,
replacement of any part of the property in respect of which no compensation is
payable.
(3) If, at any time
when a payment is to be made out of the said Fund, the sum standing to the
credit of the Fund is less than the sum required for the making of that
payment, an amount equal to deficiency shall be paid into the Fund as an
advance out of general revenues.
(4) If, at any time,
the amount standing to the credit of the Fund exceeds the sum which, in the
opinion of the Central Government, is likely to be required for the making of
payments out of the Fund, the excess shall be paid into general revenues.
(S) The Central
Government shall prepare in such form and manner as may be prescribed, and
shall publish either annually or at such intervals as may be prescribed, an
account of all sums received into and paid out of the Fund.
(6) .Notwithstanding
anything contained in subsection (1), the Central government may establish two
or more War Risks Insurance Funds each to cover one or more Schemes under this
Ordinance and the provisions of this section shall apply to each such Fund.

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
18. Power of Central
Government to extend Ordinance to certain insurance Projects.-(1) The
Central Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, declare that
the provisions of this Ordinance and of any Scheme made thereunder relating to
factories shall apply. to the insuring against war risks of -
(a) the machinery above ground
appertaining to mines, as defined in the Mines Act, 1923 (IV of 1923),
(b) the distribution systems of
gas supply undertakings, or
(c) the whole or a specified
part of the distribution and transmission systems, sub-stations, switch houses
and transformer houses of electric supply undertakings generally or of
specified electric supply undertakings as they apply to property insurable
under this Ordinance which appertains to a factory.
(2) In interpreting this
Ordinance applied by a notification under clause (a) of subsection (1) to
mines, references to the owner of a factory shall be read as references to the
owner or agent of a mine as defined in the Mines Act, 1923 (IV of 1923), and
references to the occupier of a factory shall be read as references to the
manager of a mine for the purposes of that Act.

Power to call information

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965
ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 9th September 1965]
No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
20. Power to call
information.-(1) Any person authorised in this behalf by the Central
Government may, for the purpose of ascertain ing whether or not any goods or
property required to be insured by this Ordinance has been so insured, or for
the purpose of determining the insurable value of any goods or property
insured, or required or proposed to be insured, under this Ordinance, or for
the purpose of assessing the damage suffered by any goods or property insured
under this Ordinance,-
.
(a) require the owner or
occupier of any goods and property, or any person carrying on in Pakistan the
business of any kind of insurance or of selling goods to submit to him such
accounts, books or other documents or to furnish to him such information as he
may reasonably consider necessary, or
(b) at any reasonable time-
(i) enter into any premises
occupied or otherwise used by any such per son or any premises containing or
comprising any goods or property insur able under this Ordinance.
(ii) inspect any such premises
and goods contained therein, and
(iii) require any
person found therein or thereon whom he believes to be in possession of, or
otherwise capable of furnishing, information relevant to his investigation,
furnish him such information as he may reason ably think necessary.
(2) Whoever wilfully obstructs
any person in the exercise of his powers under subsection (1) or fails without
reasonable cause to comply with anything required of him thereunder shall; in
respect o(' each such obstruction
or failure, be punishable with fine which may extend to
one thousand rupees.
(3) Whoever, in purporting to
comply with his obligations under sub section (I), knowingly or recklessly
makes a statement false in material particular, shall be punishable with fine
which may extend to one thousand rupees.
sections.punishment:
punishable with fine which may extend to
one thousand rupees.

Restriction on carrying on certain insurance business

ORDINANCE XXVI OF 1965
WAR RISKS INSURANCE ORDINANCE, 1965

No. F. 24(1)/65-Pub.-The
following Ordinance made by the President on the 9th September, 1965, is hereby
published for general information :-
21. Restriction on carrying
on certain insurance business.-(I) After the date on which any Scheme or
part of any Scheme is put into operation, no person shall, except -a person
authorized by the Central Government as their agents to issue policies in
pursuance of such scheme, carry on the business of insuring against war risks
any goods or property required to be insured under this Ordinance.
(2) Whoever contravenes the
provisions of subsection (1) shall be punishable with fine which may extend to
five thousand rupees and with a further fine which may extend to one thousand
rupees for every day after the first on which the contravention continues.
sections.punishment:
punishable with fine which may extend to
five thousand rupees and with a further fine which may extend to one thousand
rupees for every day after the first on which the contravention continues.
